facts.fact: The National Department of Health reports that the Online Birth Registration roll-out was completed in 47 health facilities in 2024/25, added to 252 completed in 2023/24, bringing to 299 the health facilities that can register births and issue birth certificates, against 1,445 public health facilities with maternity wards identified as in scope in 2019.

The National Department of Health reports that from 2021 to 2022 the project established functional Online Birth Registration infrastructure, with a dedicated network, in 161 health facilities, to which full-time Home Affairs officials were allocated to provide birth registration services.

The National Department of Health describes the Online Birth Registration System in health facilities as registering births and issuing birth certificates; it mentions no death registration through the system.

The National Department of Health states that births are registered and certificates issued at the health facility itself, by full-time Home Affairs officials posted there, through a system it calls online and for which a dedicated network infrastructure was installed; it does not name the register the record is held in.

The National Department of Health states that the Department of Home Affairs and the health department run the Online Birth Registration roll-out together, with Home Affairs officials providing the registration service in the facilities.
